short: Conformer back-end on raw inputs (M06) and Transformer LM (M07) are standard: raw-input AVSR predates it, and the Conformer gain is one unrepeated step confounded with a decoder swap.
position: The paper [@ma2021conformers] changes the recognition back-end (M06: Conformer encoders trained jointly with ResNet-18 front-ends on raw pixels and waveforms) and the language model (M07: Transformer instead of recurrent). Both are standard. Raw-input end-to-end audio-visual training predates it [@petridis2018e2e], and the Conformer, absent from every dated ledger study before it (Appendix), is credited from one LRS2 visual-only ablation step that also swaps the decoder (Table 2). The recipe became a template: the same group's [later] revision cut LRS3 visual-only WER from 43.3% to 35.1% (best of ten runs) on the same 595 h by changing the recipe [@ma2022multilingual], and [later] Auto-AVSR reached 19.1% from 3,448 h [@ma2023autoavsr], so both recipe and data moved the number (inference). The main overreach is crediting the Conformer while the largest measured step is end-to-end training (Table 2); no result reports repeated runs (§4).
